note: Observe tools expose CONDITIONS only (weather/fuels/terrain/spread/resources/map). The fire type, the matching tactic, the blow-up/danger zone, and the evac zone are hidden truth — never surfaced by an observe tool. The grader keys off whether the tactic matched the fire type and whether crews were kept out of the danger zone.

A.label: wind-driven crown fire, slope aligned with a frontal wind shift

weather.forecastShift: Dry cold front arrives ~1500: wind backs to NW at 30 gusting 50, RH crashes to 8%. Expect rapid head-fire run and long-range spotting.

fuels.fuelModel: TL/TU timber-understory with continuous ladder fuels into closed canopy
fuels.canopyContinuity: closed canopy, heavy ladder fuels — torching and crown runs already observed

spread.rateOfSpread: fast and accelerating; active crown runs
spread.note: Head fire is crowning and throwing spots well ahead of the flaming front.

terrain.feature: steep chute that aligns with the forecast NW wind — chimney effect
terrain.slopeWindAlignment: ALIGNED — slope + post-frontal wind both push fire up this chute

zones.role: values-at-risk — Pinecrest subdivision (~120 homes) directly above the head

terrain.feature: wildland-urban interface on the ridge above Z3

zones.role: anchor — wide ridgetop road with a dozer-improved fuel break

terrain.feature: ridgetop road / existing fuel break, defensible

truth.dangerReason: Z3 is a steep chute aligned with the post-frontal wind (chimney) with an active crown run above it, and Z4 is the subdivision directly downwind of the head — both are blow-up / no-engagement zones once the front arrives.

B.label: slow grass/surface fire, light wind, no canopy

weather.forecastShift: Stable. Onshore flow building this evening will further raise RH; no wind shift expected this operational period.

fuels.fuelModel: GR1/GR2 short cured grass, no overstory
fuels.canopyContinuity: no canopy — surface grass only, no ladder fuels, no torching

spread.rateOfSpread: moderate at the flaming front, backing easily
spread.note: Low flame lengths; the perimeter is workable directly with hand tools and engines.

zones.role: isolated ranch outbuilding well off the flank

terrain.feature: mowed defensible space around the structure

zones.role: two-track ranch road along the flank

terrain.feature: road usable as a direct anchor

truth.dangerReason: Low flame lengths, no slope-wind alignment, no canopy and stable weather — the perimeter can be worked directly and there is no blow-up zone this period.

C.label: wind-driven crown fire in a box canyon (rotated terrain/numbers)

weather.forecastShift: Down-canyon wind reversal expected after dark (~2000): flow shifts to W 25 gusting 45, channeling straight into the box canyon. Plume-driven runs likely.

fuels.fuelModel: TU5 dense conifer reproduction with heavy ladder fuels
fuels.canopyContinuity: dense closed canopy, continuous ladder fuels — group torching and short crown runs observed

spread.note: Crown fire with prolific spotting; canyon will align with the evening wind reversal.

zones.role: right flank climbing the canyon wall
active head deep in the box canyon

terrain.feature: BOX CANYON head — no safe egress, aligns with the evening down-canyon reversal
terrain.slopeWindAlignment: ALIGNED — classic box-canyon chimney once the wind reverses

terrain.feature: campground on the canyon floor below the head
terrain.slopeWindAlignment: in the path of a down-canyon run

zones.role: anchor — county road across the canyon mouth

terrain.feature: paved road / natural fuel break at the canyon mouth, defensible

truth.dangerReason: Z3 is a box-canyon head that aligns with the forecast evening down-canyon wind reversal (chimney, no egress) under an active crown run, and Z6 is the campground on the canyon floor in the path of a down-canyon run — both are blow-up / no-engagement zones.
